title: Fair Work Amendment (A Living Wage) Bill 2018
short_title: Fair Work Amendment (A Living Wage) Bill 2018

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: This bill would raise Australia's lowest legal pay rate to a level defined as a living wage.
The Fair Work Commission would set a phase-in schedule of up to six years and publish it, then conduct annual reviews with possible departures only in exceptional circumstances.
The target is 60% of the median full-time weekly earnings calculated by the Australian Bureau of Statistics.
changes: Increase the national minimum wage to 60% of the median full-time weekly wage.
Require the Fair Work Commission to determine a phase-in period no longer than six years.
Require the Fair Work Commission to publish a timetable for the phase-in.
Oblige the Fair Work Commission to consider factors such as reducing inequality and economic conditions in setting the timetable.
Allow the Fair Work Commission to deviate from the planned phase-in only in exceptional circumstances during annual wage reviews.
summary.affected: Low-paid employees and their employers, the Fair Work Commission, and the Australian Bureau of Statistics.
